title: Harvest Pricing: Plans, Per-Seat Cost & Fees (2026)
summary: Harvest pricing on three plans depends on per-seat rates, but seat counts and plan limits also affect your costs.
body_markdown:
## Fix Harvest Seat and Timesheet Gaps with Activepieces


Activepieces is an MIT-licensed automation platform with 750+ integrations, and it runs the checks nobody remembers to run. It's not a Harvest alternative, and it doesn't change what Harvest charges you.


Doing nothing has a price of its own: a seat nobody uses renews every month at $11 on Teams monthly billing, and a missing timesheet holds up an invoice.[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) connects to Harvest and handles three jobs:


- A timesheet reminder that nudges people with missing hours before the week closes.
- A monthly inactive-seat check that lists anyone with no logged time, so you can remove them before the next bill.
- A handoff that passes approved hours to your invoicing step, so nobody retypes them.


A per-seat licence turns every new hire into a line item, which is why access ends up with a chosen few while everyone else waits.


Activepieces meters by consumption instead: credits follow usage, and unlimited flows come on every plan, including Free with its 1,000 credits a month, so adding a person costs nothing until they run an automation.


Alan and Funding Societies both run production automation on Activepieces. Its pricing page lists the credit allowances and the $0 Free plan, so you can work out what your own checks would use before building anything.


Top to bottom, the steps run in order, each connected to the next by a vertical line.


Your seat check has the same shape: a monthly trigger, a condition that asks whether someone logged hours, and a message to whoever approves seats. Nothing in it needs engineering vocabulary, just a sequence you can read from top to bottom.


What the tool itself costs is flat.[Activepieces lists](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) a Free plan at $0 a month, so you can build the inactive-seat check and see whether it catches anything before you spend a dollar.


$20 a month gets you Plus, a small fixed line you can weigh against one unused Harvest seat, so the economic case hinges on whether your Harvest account has idle capacity.


$200 a month buys Team, which only makes sense once several people rely on these workflows.


Add people to the plan and the cost doesn't rise, which is the opposite of how Harvest bills.


Start on Free and let one month's check show what it finds.
